Your **eQ-3 MAX!** heating system in Gladys, through the local port of the
**MAX! Cube** (TCP 62910) on your network, without any cloud:

- **radiator thermostats** (MAX! Heating Thermostat and Thermostat+): room
  **temperature** (when the Cube gives one), **setpoint**, **mode** (auto,
  heating, off), **MAX! mode** (auto, manual, vacation, boost), **heating
  state** and **valve opening** (%), **battery low**, **radio link error**;
- **wall thermostats** (MAX! Wall Thermostat): **temperature**, **setpoint**,
  **mode**, **MAX! mode**, battery, link;
- **window contacts** (MAX! Shutter Contact): **open / closed**, battery,
  link;
- the **Cube** itself: **radio duty cycle** (%) and **free command slots**.

> **This integration has never been tested with a real Cube.** This first
> version was written from the protocol description (Bouni/max-cube-protocol)
> and the python-maxcube-api library (the one of Home Assistant), and tested
> only against a fake Cube. Say on the Gladys forum what works and what does
> not.

Unofficial integration, not affiliated with eQ-3. The MAX! hardware is no
longer made, but it remains widely installed; the eQ-3 portal is not used.

## What you need

- A **MAX! Cube** (the LAN gateway) on your network, with its devices already
  paired and sorted by room in the MAX! software (the names of the rooms and
  devices come from there). Push buttons (MAX! Eco Switch) are ignored.
- A Cube accepts **one client at a time**. By default, Gladys keeps its
  connection open: the MAX! software cannot connect meanwhile. Untick **Keep
  the connection open** so that Gladys only opens a connection for the time
  of a read or a command; the MAX! software can then connect between two
  reads.

## Configuration

- **Cube address**: its IP address on your network (`192.168.1.40`), shown by
  your router or the MAX! software; a port may follow (62910 by default).
  Prefer the IP address: a `.local` name (mDNS) does not resolve inside the
  container of the integration. Give the Cube a fixed address in your router;
  if it changes, type the new one: the devices and their history are kept
  (they are known by their serial numbers). No password: the Cube asks for
  none on its local port.
- **Allow the setpoint commands** and **Allow the mode commands**: off by
  default (see Commands).
- **Keep the connection open**: ticked by default (see above).
- **Language of the devices**: French (default) or English.

Then open the **Discover** tab and create the devices to follow. The devices
are named `Room - Name` after the MAX! software. The **Test the connection**
button reads the Cube and lists what it shows; it never reads the Cube again
less than a minute after the previous read (it then shows the last read), but
it does not wait for the retry pause after a failure.

## Readings

- The Cube is read every **minute** (its own memory, no radio traffic: the
  MAX! devices report to the Cube at their own pace, and the Cube keeps their
  last values). With the connection kept open, a device that reports to the
  Cube is shown at once. Only the values that change are sent to Gladys (and
  each one at least every 10 minutes).
- The **temperature** of a radiator thermostat is only given by the Cube now
  and then (when the valve moves, in auto or manual mode); the one of a wall
  thermostat is at each read (per the protocol description). A device the Cube has not heard yet (no values) shows
  as **unreachable** and the status says so.
- The **mode** follows the modes of Gladys: **auto** (3) when the thermostat
  follows its weekly programme, **heating** (1) in manual, boost or vacation,
  **off** (0) when the setpoint is 4.5 °C (valve closed). The **MAX! mode**
  (text: `auto`, `manual`, `vacation`, `boost`) gives the detail.
- The window contact is **1 closed, 0 open** (the opening sensor of Gladys).
- Only the values the Cube marks **valid** are shown: a device whose entry is
  not valid or not initialized, or that reports a **radio link error**, only
  shows its flags (battery low, link error), shows as unreachable, and the
  status says so. The radio budget of the Cube is only shown when less than
  10 minutes old (the Cube resets it every hour).
- A message of the Cube that cannot be read for one device (its
  configuration, an entry too short) does not stop the reading of the
  others. Two devices on the same radio address are left out (the log gives
  their number).
- The names of the rooms and devices are read again at each new connection
  (every 6 hours at the latest with the connection kept).

## Commands

By default, Gladys only **reads**, and can **stop** a thermostat (the stop
needs no option). Once an option is ticked, the dashboard, the scenes, the
voice assistants (Siri / HomeKit, Alexa, Google Home) and the Thermostat
service of Gladys can also set the setpoint or switch to heating or auto. As
the MAX! software does, each command is sent to the **whole room** of the
thermostat (the thermostats of a room are linked).

### Off (mode 0)

Off puts the thermostat in manual at **4.5 °C**, the "off" setpoint of MAX!
(valve closed). It needs **no option**, no bounds and no values of the
device: only the device in the list of the Cube. It is sent even when the
device seems off already. It goes **before** the other commands:

- the commands of the same room asked before it and not sent yet are
  cancelled ("cancelled: a stop was asked");
- a read of the Cube without answer for 1 s, or a connection whose greeting
  has been silent for 1 s (not a byte), is cut (a younger read is waited for: the Cube
  answers it in a few milliseconds);
- it only waits for the answer to a command already sent (2 s at most);
- after a connection is closed, it waits for the Cube to free its slot (it
  accepts one client), then opens again; whatever keeps it from leaving (a
  connection refused or closed, a greeting that does not come, a previous
  command without answer) is tried again every 250 ms, within the 3.5 s that
  follow the command.

The thermostat applies its own frost protection as described by eQ-3: check
the manual of your device before leaving a radiator off in winter.

An off command that could not leave within these 3.5 s **is not dropped**:
Gladys answers "not sent yet", the status of the integration says so, and it
leaves at the next read of the Cube (5 s later), 3 tries at most. Off is
**refused** only when: the address of the Cube is not set or the
configuration is not loaded yet; the configuration changes during the
command; the device is no longer paired with the Cube. Once sent, it can be
**discarded by the Cube** (radio budget of the hour used up, or no free slot)
or **queued** by it; Gladys says so.

It is then **checked**: the Cube is read again 5 s, 30 s, 1 min and 2 min
after it. When the thermostat does not show it 1 min after the send, it is
sent again, 3 times at most (not while the fresh radio budget of the Cube is
at 90 % or more); when it is still not applied 2 min after the last send
(radio budget included), the logs and the status of the integration say so
("the stop was not applied by ..."), until the device shows it. A newer
command accepted for the same room (setpoint, heating, auto), sent or already
so, replaces the stop: it is then no longer sent, nor sent again.

### Setpoint, heating, auto

- **Allow the setpoint commands**: the **setpoint** of a radiator or wall
  thermostat, **5 to 30 °C**, rounded to the half degree (the resolution of
  the thermostat), within the bounds set on **every thermostat of the room**
  (the Cube gives them); a value outside is refused, never brought back into
  the bounds. In auto mode, the setpoint holds until the next switch point of
  the weekly programme; otherwise it puts the thermostat in manual (a boost or
  a vacation under way ends).
- **Allow the mode commands (auto, heating)**:
  - **auto** (3): back to the weekly programme of the device;
  - **heating** (1): manual at the current setpoint, or at the comfort
    temperature set on the device when the valve was closed;
  - **cooling** (2): refused, a MAX! thermostat does not cool.
- Just before acting, Gladys **asks the Cube for its live values** and
  decides on that read only. One of these commands is **not sent** when:
  - the option is unticked (checked when the command arrives and again just
    before sending), or the configuration is not loaded yet;
  - the value is not a number from 5 to 30 °C, or the mode is not 1 or 3;
  - the thermostat is off and only the setpoint is allowed (a setpoint would
    start it again: "switch it to heating or auto");
  - the device is no longer paired; the Cube has no values for it; its
    values are marked not valid or it reports a radio link error;
  - the bounds of the thermostats of the room leave no value; heating needs
    the comfort temperature and the Cube does not give it;
  - the radio budget of the Cube (given less than 10 min ago) reaches 90 %
    or it has no free slot (the command would wait up to an hour);
  - the read fails or does not end in time, the configuration changes, or a
    stop of the same room is asked meanwhile;
  - the value asked is already the one of **every** thermostat of the room
    (nothing to do, the command is acknowledged).
- These commands run one after the other (one Cube, one connection).
- A command not seen on the device 2 min after its send is said in the logs
  (not sent again).

### Delays

The delays are measured on the monotonic clock of the container (a change of
the time of day does not change them). When a command cannot be sent within
the 3.5 s that follow its arrival, nothing is sent and Gladys shows a
failure. Once sent, Gladys gets an answer at most 4.3 s after the command
arrived: "accepted by the Cube" when the Cube answered that it passes it over
the radio, "sent, without confirmation" when it has not answered yet,
"queued" or "discarded" after its answer. The Cube does not confirm that the
thermostat applied the command: it is checked on the follow-up reads (see
above); the value shown is always the one the Cube gives, never the one
asked.

The weekly programme, the boost, the vacation mode, the comfort and eco
temperatures, the temperature offset and the pairing stay in the MAX!
software.

## Connection problems

- **Cube unreachable** or not answering: every device shows as unreachable;
  new try after 1 min, then less and less often up to every 10 min (never
  faster than the normal read). The most common cause: another client (the
  MAX! software, another integration) holds the connection of the Cube.
- **This address does not answer like a MAX! Cube**: the address or the port
  (62910) is wrong, or another service answers.
- After a restart of the integration, the reading loop does not read the
  Cube again less than a minute after the previous read (the time of the last
  read is kept in `/data`); a command reads it just before acting, and the
  reads that follow a command take place 5 s, 30 s, 1 min and 2 min after it.
- The logs hold nothing of what the Cube sends (no serial numbers, names or
  values): only our own words, the kind of device ("thermostat", "wall") and
  numbers (no connection, no answer in time...). The status of the
  integration names the devices (room and name) whose stop was not applied.

## Limits

- One Cube per integration.
- No boost, vacation mode, weekly programme, comfort / eco temperatures,
  pairing or removal of devices from Gladys.
- Push buttons (Eco Switch) are not published.
- Never tested with a real Cube.

## Cómo instalar MAX! Cube en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: MAX! Cube aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-maxcube:0.1.2`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-maxcube](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-maxcube).

MAX! Cube requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

MAX! Cube es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
